claims.assertion: The trip was a metered RydeTAXI ride, so extra kilometres were billed directly to the rider: 9.61 km was charged against an optimal route of 3.9 km, +5.7 km (+144%), and the fare shows $7.99 billed as excess distance alone.

The GPS track contains two off-route segments: 14:10–14:15 adding 1.85 km (2.68 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.83 km) and 14:17–14:29 adding 2.87 km (3.64 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.77 km), together 4.72 km of added distance.

The rider's only route-related message before the trip was agreement to the driver's proposal to 'go round by Cavenagh' (driver 14:01, rider 14:02), a specific named-road authorisation that at most covers driving on Cavenagh; nothing in the record places either driven off-route segment at the location of that named road, so the segments cannot be exempted as agreed driving on that road.

The rider's 14:02 message asked only for 'a quick 7-Eleven on the way' and named no place, and the record contains no driver message before the segments telling the rider which 7-Eleven he had chosen, so the rider's consent reached only a short stop, not the choice of a stop that pulled the car far off the route.

The only stationary period away from the route is 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24, ~3.0 km from the pickup and ~2.1 km from the drop-off, sitting inside the second off-route segment (14:17–14:29), and the driver's own statement says the 7-Eleven he chose is the one he knows on Beach Road — a place the rider never named.

The driver's justification of congestion is only partly supported: an accident on Orchard Road was reported at 13:52 and lies 0 m from the optimal route, and Orchard Road was in speed band 1 during 14:00–14:10, but that covers only the start of the trip and nothing justifies the second off-route segment, which ran 14:17–14:29 and reached 1553 m off the optimal route.
Because the trip is metered, the refund is the unbilled-for distance on the unexempted segments at this trip's per-km rate: 4.72 km × $1.4100/km = $6.66 (1.85 × 1.41 = $2.61 and 2.87 × 1.41 = $4.05).

The waiting charge of $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) also falls within the unexempted diversion, since the 4 min 10 s stationary period corresponds to the far-away 7-Eleven stop inside the second off-route segment, and that stop was not the place the rider asked for.

The driver's account is contradicted by the system records: he claims the rider agreed to go round by Cavenagh, but no record ties either off-route segment to Cavenagh Road, and he admits he chose the Beach Road 7-Eleven himself, which no rider message asked for.

A flag_account review is warranted in addition to the refund: the driver has 3 disputes and 1 upheld in the last 90 days, and if this case is upheld it becomes a second upheld dispute within the window.

weaknesses: The rider did agree to the driver's proposal to go round by Cavenagh (F10, F11) and asked for a 7-Eleven stop, and traffic evidence supports part of the driver's story — an accident on Orchard Road 0 m from the optimal route (F18) with Orchard Road in speed band 1 during 14:00–14:10 (F15) — so the first off-route segment (F4) is the segment where the driver has his best RD-4 case and my 'untied' reading of it depends on the absence of any record placing the car on Cavenagh Road (G13).

The rider's message 'a quick 7-Eleven on the way' (F11) does consent to a stop, so the other side can argue the diversion to a 7-Eleven was within the scope of the rider's own request under RD-3(a)/(b), and the judge may read the stationary period (F2) as the requested stop rather than as a detour to be refunded.

Nothing in the record names the road actually driven on either off-route segment, so the judge may find the Cavenagh agreement 'undetermined' (G13) rather than unexempted, which would send the amount to a human rather than produce a clean RD-2 figure.
The $1.08 waiting charge (F7) is a metered time unit and RD-3(c) says metered waiting is charged as billed, so my claim to that $1.08 is the weakest part of the money claim.
The rider's account age, 4.9 rating and zero prior disputes (F20) help credibility but decide nothing, and no profile fact can be used to establish the deviation itself.

claims.assertion: The rider herself chose to send the car via Cavenagh: at 14:01 the driver asked 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' (F10) and at 14:02 the rider answered 'Sure.' (F11) — a rider message before the first off-route segment, which began at 14:10 (F4).

Independently of consent, there was a reasonable cause to leave Orchard Road: an accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed, was reported at 13:52 at a point 0 m from the optimal route (F18), while Orchard Road was in speed band 1 (0-9 km/h) at 14:00-14:10 (F15) — i.e. the incident pre-dates the trip and sits on the replaced stretch of the optimal route.

The 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20-14:24 (F2) is the 7-Eleven stop the rider asked for at 14:02 (F11) and the driver accepted at 14:03 (F12); a rider-requested stop is reviewed under RD-3, not as a detour, and its duration is chargeable on RydeTAXI under RD-3(c) — the $1.08 waiting billed (F7) reflects 4.2 min at meter waiting rate.

To the extent any km are held unexcused, the refund on this RydeTAXI trip can only be the metered mileage units of those segments: the fare shows 5.67 km of excess billed at the trip's per-km rate of $1.4100 (F6), derived from the metered breakdown of $25.81 (F9); the waiting $1.08 (F7) and the platform fee $1.47 (F9) are published components and are not refundable under RD-2.

No additional account action is warranted: although the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days (F21), it is a no-show dispute with 0 route disputes upheld (F21), so the RD-6 'repeated route deviation' precondition is not met.

The complaint contains no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — the rider's message is a fare/routing objection only (F14 is the driver's own statement), so SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is not engaged.

weaknesses: The most damaging record for us: the second off-route segment 14:17-14:29 added 2.87 km and went up to 1553 m from the optimal route (F5), and the stationary stop at 14:20-14:24 was 2995 m from pickup / 2098 m from drop-off (F2) — that geography is consistent with the driver's own written admission that he stopped at 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14), which the rider did not name (F11).

We have no record that ties the driven roads to Cavenagh Road: there is no stop on Cavenagh, no message placing the car there, and no road-name fact for the driven path, so the rider's 'Sure' (F11) is at best a named-road agreement with nothing tying the segment to it, and the judge may find those segments undetermined (G13).

The Cavenagh exchange (F10-F11) pre-dates only the first segment (F4, 14:10-14:15); the 14:17-14:29 segment (F5) is separated from it by the stop and may be read as the driver's own errand rather than the agreed route.

Traffic only corroborates the first segment: the accident (F18) is on Orchard Road and Orchard's band-1 record is 14:00-14:10 (F15), while nothing in the traffic facts justifies the 14:17-14:29 loop or the Beach Road stop.
The transit time was 26.5 min against a 7.7 min estimate (F3) and actual distance 9.6 km against 3.9 km (F1), figures the rider will use to argue the whole excess was unexplained.

points.response: The 'Sure' at 14:02 (F11) is a yes to a driver's ask that named a road, so it is a named-road authorisation, not a general route licence, and RD-5 requires a record tying the driven segment to that named road; no fact places the car on Cavenagh — F4's segment runs 14:10-14:15 up to 803 m off the optimal route and the road names in the record (F15, F16, F17, F18) are Orchard, Bras Basah, Bayfront and the Cavenagh/Orchard junction, none of which locates the driven path — so F4 is at most named_road_untied (G13), and F5 is not covered by the 14:02 message at all.

RD-4 requires the traffic evidence to be directed at the replaced stretch of optimal route and to cover the segment in time: the accident (F18) and Orchard's band-1 record 14:00-14:10 (F15) reach only the start of the trip, while the unexempted segment F5 ran 14:17-14:29 and strayed 1553 m from the route, and Bayfront Avenue (F17) is a category-3 road at band 3, not the optimal corridor at all.

The rider asked for 'a quick 7-Eleven on the way' and named no place (F11), and the driver's own statement shows he chose the store himself — 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F14), which the rider never named — so under RD-3(b) the consent is a consent to stop, not to that route change; the stop also sits 2995 m from the pickup inside the 14:17-14:29 off-route segment (F2, F5), and the $1.08 waiting (F7) is time spent on that unexempted diversion.

We accept the refund is limited to meter mileage units of the unexempted segments, but the arithmetic is 1.85 km + 2.87 km = 4.72 km at the trip's own rate of $1.4100/km (F6), i.e. $6.66, not the $2.87 offered, which refunds only the second segment and leaves the first unexempted segment unpaid.
